purpose: longitudinal SPECT registration where the two series no longer show the same thing: lesions appear, change size and disappear between timepoints
content: egg-shaped body; background cloud (band-limited random Fourier series) + organ uptake in the `tex` arm, nothing in the `smooth` arm; up to 25 spherical lesions

content.t25: 25 lesions: the 20 baseline sites resized, plus 5 new
content.t00: the same 25 sites, faded to just above background (response)

transform.id: identity — the truth is that nothing moved

background.smooth: no background structure at all (observability floor)

interesting_pairs: t20-id-* vs t25-*-*   : 20 lesions -> 25, all resized (moderate content change)
t20-id-* vs t00-*-*   : 20 lesions -> none (extreme content change)
t25-id-* vs t00-*-*   : disappearance only, positions unchanged
t20-id-* vs t20-*-*   : control — transform only, content identical
design.note: Compare a `tex` result only with another `tex` result. The `smooth` arm has no background structure by construction, so its numbers are a floor, not a score.

direction_convention: transform_fixed_to_moving maps a point of the FIXED series to the point of the MOVING series holding the same anatomy: q = T(p). This is the transform a registration must recover, and the one GRAPHY passes to computeFusionSlice as xf.
euler_convention: R = Rz(rz) . Ry(ry) . Rx(rx), degrees, right-handed about patient LPS, about rotation_centre_mm; identical to mat4FromEulerDeg in frontend/src/viewer/regTransform.ts
frame_of_reference: Every series declares a DIFFERENT FrameOfReferenceUID, as two SPECT sessions months apart do. An engine that branches on FoR agreement therefore takes its 'separately acquired' path for every pair here.

acquisition.order: analytic activity on a grid FINE x finer -> pre-PSF blur -> bin down -> Poisson -> post-filter. Partial-volume loss emerges from this order rather than being applied afterwards; the post-filter is what makes the noise correlated.
acquisition.noise_seeds: distinct per series, so matching noise cannot be used as a cue
acquisition.units: counts; no rescale pair is written (NM convention)

evaluation_region.note: inscribed in the egg for every z; outside it the estimate is an extrapolation

observability: lesion_measurements[].cnr is measured on the written volume. A landmark whose CNR is below ~3 is not detectable after the 10 mm effective PSF and Poisson statistics, and a large TRE there is a property of the data, not of the engine. Judge accuracy on detectable landmarks and report the rest separately.

acceptance_targets.note: inherited from fw/registration-design.md §9.1/§9.4 so the scorer has limits to print. They were set for a 1 mm CT-like phantom and are almost certainly the wrong scale for a 4.42 mm SPECT grid — fix them with measurements, not opinion.
